cvOptimizer.title: CV Optimizer Pro
cvOptimizer.sub: An agent system that interviews you and builds a CV you can defend in a real interview.
cvOptimizer.shot: Screenshot of the coach interview and the feedback card
problem: When I wrote my CV I didn't know what to tell. There were things I did every day and didn't value. Leading 2 people was one of them.
The tools I tried did the opposite. They inflated everything, and that falls apart at the first interview question.
cvOptimizer.pipelineAria: The interview with the AI coach builds the profile, the auditor reviews what has no backing, it is matched against the job posting and an ATS CV comes out.
steps: An AI coach asks about your experience. Every answer leads to a new question and it never repeats itself. If you already have a CV, you upload the PDF or DOCX and it pre-fills the profile.
An agent reviews what you said and flags what you can't back up or what you're underselling.
You paste a job posting, see the fit and generate the tailored CV with its keyword report.
decisions: The auditor has the last word. An achievement with no backing doesn't make it into the CV.
One column, Arial and no graphics, so ATS systems read all of it.
Each interview phase has a turn limit and shows progress, so it never drags on.
cvOptimizer.result: I use it with my own profile. The CV I apply with today came out of it, and the interview is what made me see that leading 2 devs was an achievement.

jobHunter.title: Job Hunter Platform
jobHunter.sub: A platform that checks job boards for me, ranks listings against my profile and builds the CV for each one.
jobHunter.shot: Screenshot of the dashboard with the listings ranking
problem: Job hunting meant checking the same boards every day and reading listings that didn't fit me.
I wanted a system to do that first pass and leave me only the ones worth reading.
jobHunter.pipelineAria: Three job boards are checked every two hours with Celery, listings are stored in PostgreSQL, OpenAI scores the fit and the result goes to a dashboard.
steps: Three scrapers check RemoteOK, WeWorkRemotely and GetOnBoard every 2 hours with Celery Beat and store listings in a common format.
OpenAI compares each listing with my profile and assigns a fit score.
From the dashboard I pick a listing and generate a tailored CV, with a version built for ATS.
decisions: It runs on Celery with Redis, so no slow board holds up the dashboard.
Each scraper maps its board to the same PostgreSQL model. Adding a board means writing one new class.
Listings, profile, CV, applications and notifications each have their own FastAPI router.
jobHunter.result: It runs fully on local Docker Compose: API, worker, database and dashboard.
